To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the liver plays a role in the control of feeding.
the liver is a site of integration of oral and gastrointestinal factors which are important in the control of feeding.
the liver, when considered as part of a system which includes the mouth, gastrointestinal tract, and brain, is important in the control of feeding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the liver in the regulation of food intake.
the role of the liver in the overall control of feeding.
the role of the liver in feeding and with the integration of peripheral and central events which are involved in the control of feeding.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the liver is involved in feeding but its role is not clear and needs further study.
the liver has an important role in the control of feeding but that this role is probably not a direct one.
the liver is not involved in feeding.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the liver is not the sole controller of feeding but it does play an important role in the overall control of food intake.
the liver is an organ of metabolic regulation and that it can influence feeding.
the liver is important in the control of feeding but not in the control of the feeding response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liver is a key player in the brain-gut axis.
the liver is not the only place where the brain can get metabolic information about food intake.
the liver is not the master controller of food intake.
